newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ISRAEL PROBES AUSTRALIAN DEATHS AT JEWISH OLYMPICS.
newsitem.headline: ISRAEL PROBES AUSTRALIAN DEATHS AT JEWISH OLYMPICS.

text.p: Israel on Tuesday named a commission to probe the collapse of a pedestrian bridge that killed two Australians at the opening ceremonies of a sporting event popularly known as the Jewish Olympics.

"Although it may be of little comfort to the bereaved families, please be assured that we are conducting a thorough investigation into this disaster," Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu wrote in a condolence message to Australian Prime Minister John Howard.

Israeli officials said a public commission would submit its findings within a week, before the 51-nation Maccabiah Games end. The seven-member group will be chaired by retired Brigadier Ishai Dotan, former chief engineer of the Israeli army.

Competitors from the 370-member Australian team were walking across the bridge over the Yarkon River on Monday ready to lead a march into the Ramat Gan Stadium near Tel Aviv for the opening of the games when the metal and wood structure buckled.
Two Australians from Sydney, ten-pin bowler Greg Small,37, and 50-year-old Yetty Bennet, section manager of the men's bowling team, were killed and 43 delegation members were injured.

"On behalf of the government, the citizens of Israel and on my own behalf, I wish to express our profound sorrow at the tragic accident which occurred just before the official opening of the 15th Maccabiah yesterday," Netanyahu wrote in the message to Howard released by his office.
The engineer who planned and inspected the pedestrian bridge was questioned by police on Tuesday. Police said there was no suspicion of foul play.

"I demanded, and those who commissioned the bridge agreed, that someone would stand at its entrance and not allow more than 100 people to cross at one time," the engineer, Micha Bar-Ilan, told Israel's Channel Two television.
Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said he knew of no such request but the matter would be investigated. The Maccabiah organising committee commissioned the bridge from a private company.

"We were walking across. All of a sudden we heard a bang," Australia team manager Harry Purcell told reporters. "And then all of a sudden in slow motion it just collapsed in the middle and we started to slide."
The quadrennial games were postponed for a day of mourning. More than 5,500 Jewish athletes will compete in the games when they get under way on Wednesday and wear black armbands of mourning.
Organisers dropped the march of national teams but a public storm erupted over the decision to proceed with entertainment for the 50,000 spectators present for the opening ceremony.
Australian delegation leaders said individual members were given the option of returning home but it appeared most would choose to stay and compete.
